sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Three primary techniques exist for grounding LLMs with domain knowledge: **RAG** (dynamic retrieval at inference time), **Fine-tuning** (baking knowledge into model weights), and **Prompt Stuffing** (inserting all relevant text directly into the prompt). Each serves different use cases. Fine-tuning excels at teaching the model behavioral patterns, tone, or reasoning styles — it's expensive but produces a model that "thinks" in your domain. Prompt stuffing works for small, stable knowledge bases that fit in context (< ~50 pages) and offers zero infrastructure overhead. RAG is the gold standard for large, dynamic, access-controlled knowledge bases where citations matter, as it scales to millions of documents with fresh retrieval and per-document access control. In 2026 production systems, the dominant pattern is a **combination**: fine-tune for behavior, RAG for knowledge.

diagrams.title: RAG, fine-tuning or prompt stuffing?
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  S(["What does the model lack?"]) --> K{"Knowledge or behaviour?"}
  K -- "facts that change, private docs, need citations" --> R["RAG"]
  K -- "style, format, domain language, a skill" --> F["Fine-tuning"]
  K -- "a few pages that fit the context window" --> P["Prompt stuffing"]
  R --> B["Often: RAG for knowledge + light fine-tune for format"]
  F --> B
diagrams.explain: Use **RAG** when the problem is *knowledge*: it changes, it is private, or answers need sources. Use **fine-tuning** when the problem is *behaviour*: tone, output format, domain jargon. If everything fits in the context window, just **put it in the prompt**. Production systems often combine RAG for facts with a small fine-tune for format.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
DECISION MATRIX: RAG vs Fine-tuning vs Prompt Stuffing
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

                    PROMPT STUFFING
                    ┌─────────────┐
                    │ All docs in │
User Query ────────▶│  context    │────▶ LLM ────▶ Answer
                    │ (expensive) │
                    └─────────────┘
                    Works for: < 50 pages, stable content, prototypes
                    Fails at:  scale, cost, access control

                    RAG (RETRIEVAL-AUGMENTED)
                    ┌─────────┐   ┌──────────┐
                    │ Vector  │   │ Top-3    │
User Query ────────▶│ Search  │──▶│ Chunks   │──▶ LLM ──▶ Answer
                    │         │   │ Only     │
                    └─────────┘   └──────────┘
    ↕                     ↕
 Live Index           Updated daily
                    Works for: Large corpora, dynamic data, citations
                    Fails at:  Complex reasoning needing full context

                    FINE-TUNING
                    ┌─────────────┐
                    │  Model with │
User Query ────────▶│  knowledge  │────▶ Answer (no retrieval)
                    │  in weights │
                    └─────────────┘
                    Works for: Style/format, stable knowledge, low latency
                    Fails at:  Fresh data, attribution, access control

WHEN TO USE WHICH:
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Knowledge changes frequently?      → RAG
Need source attribution?           → RAG
Knowledge base > 50 pages?         → RAG
Need specific output format?       → Fine-tune (+ RAG for facts)
Latency must be < 200ms?           → Fine-tune
Small stable internal FAQ?         → Prompt stuffing (prototype)
Production multi-tenant system?    → RAG + access control
Best accuracy on complex domain?   → Fine-tune + RAG (RAFT pattern)
```
